title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
claim: Ln(III) 4f charge density in the Ising-limit ground state is ellipsoidal rather than spherical, and for oblate ions such as Tb(III) and Dy(III) axial ligand electron density is particularly effective at generating large magnetic anisotropy.
explanation: The review summarizes Long's quadrupole/point-charge model: strong angular dependence of 4f orbitals gives nonspherical density. It lists prolate ('flat and long') ions Pm3+, Sm3+, Eu3+, Er3+, Tm3+, Yb3+, oblate ('flat') ions Ce3+, Pr3+, Nd3+, Tb3+, Dy3+, Ho3+, and isotropic Gd3+. For oblate cases exemplified by [Pc2Tb]- and [Pc2Dy]-, axial ligand electrons favor large anisotropy. Tb and Dy are further said to show remarkable anisotropy in strongly axial ligand fields because of their oblate density.
scope: Design of ligand fields for trivalent lanthanide SMMs, especially Tb and Dy phthalocyanines and other axial complexes.
conditions: The model refers to the Ising-limit ground-state charge density and an effective point-charge electrostatic picture.
caveats: The review states the axial-ligand preference explicitly for oblate Tb/Dy; it does not spell out the complementary equatorial-ligand rule for prolate ions in the readable text. Gd3+ is isotropic and is not grouped with the oblate ions.
